WildfireX implements five Discrete Mathematics modules backed by NetworkX and SymPy: (I) Combinatorics & Inclusion-Exclusion (sum/product rules, nPr, nCr, pigeonhole, derangements, rook polynomials); (II) Propositional & Predicate Logic (safe AST truth tables, equivalences, De Morgan laws, inference, finite quantifiers); (III) Generating Functions & Recurrence Relations (OGF, EGF, integer partitions, 1st/2nd-order closed-form verification); (IV) Graph Theory G=(V,E) (Handshaking Lemma sum(deg)=2|E|, VF2 isomorphism, walks/paths, Euler/Hamiltonian, planarity & coloring); (V) Trees & Algorithms (Kruskal/Prim MST, Dijkstra shortest paths, Huffman prefix-free coding, binary tree traversals, sorting).

WildfireX is an academic and environmental research prototype. Its controlled cellular automata demonstrations are educational and hypothetical. Outputs are not validated operational wildfire predictions and must not be used for emergency-response decisions. Historical satellite hotspot observations are not equivalent to confirmed fire perimeters. Real-world environmental conclusions require verified datasets, field validation and expert assessment. Satellite-detected hotspots (e.g., NASA FIRMS MODIS/VIIRS thermal anomalies) represent 375m-1000m pixel thermal detections and are NOT automatically equivalent to confirmed wildfire incidents or mapped burned-area perimeters. Geographical land-cover layers and hypothetical cellular automata outputs are stored and labeled separately.
